# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ The last week of February was positive for metals prices until the very last day of the month. Before that, all of the metals benefited from a slightly surprising acceptance of risk by the investor community and from a weakening Dollar. While platinum gained on gold, partly on sentiment and partly on the continuing supply side disruption in South Africa, fundamentals did not seem to be the prime mover for higher prices. On the 29th, a risk-driven move into the Dollar and out of commodities hit all of the precious metals hard with gold plunging almost $100 and silver nearly $3. Since then, worries over the reality of the Greek bail-out have resurfaced -again - weakening the Euro and sending precious metal prices lower again. ETF buying was positive for all four main metals over the end of February. For gold and silver, this was outweighed by very strong futures buying, suggesting that the safe haven aspects of these metals were not greatly in demand but that short term price gains were the target. In platinum and palladium, futures gains were more measured but investors showed greater confidence in the fundamental story by buying more than one tonne of each metal through the Exchange Traded Funds. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** ##### **06 March 2012** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report 06 March 2012** ### **Gold CFTC data to 28 February 2012; ETF data to 2 March 2012.** **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

8,288|1,639,139|**70,527,965**| |**02-Mar-12**|41,592,971|5,835,581|3,824,581|381,779|1,278,217|7,184,063|5,584,614|3,507,088|1,639,139|**70,828,033**| |**Change**|**291,499**|**20,289**|**-1,936**|**0**|**-69**|**37,382**|**-65,897**|**18,800**|**0**|**300,068**| The gold price climbed from $1,735 on the 21st of February to a high of $1,785 at the end of the month with assistance from gentle ETF buying, much more speculative interest in the futures market and news stories of central bank buying, as well as a faltering US Dollar. At this point, gold looked set to challenge $1,800 and press higher, perhaps threatening last year’s all-time nominal highs sooner rather than later. As we cautioned at the start of the year, however, the path higher was unlikely to be smooth. This was amply demonstrated after the release of the ECB’s long term borrowing scheme’s uptake data and Ben Bernanke’s most recent comments. Although neither was particularly surprising, something spooked the market and gold was sold down by almost $100 on the 29th to a low of $1,690. Since that point, concerns have reemerged that the Greek bail-out might not be as final as previously expected and the Dollar has strengthened against the Euro, placing the precious metals under pressure. Gold recovered to $1,725 but has since slipped to $1,687 and currently looks rather weak. Speculative interest on COMEX increased by a touch more than two million ounce in the week to the 28th of February. With positions at an extended level, a sell-off was not entirely surprising and we expect next week’s commitment of traders report to reveal a sharp contraction in speculative exposure. However, with more recent, weaker longs knocked from the market, a move higher is possible if the Euro stabilises. ETF flows of gold were marginally positive over the end of February as 300,000 more ounces were bought than were sold. Total holdings are now 70.8 million ounces, their highest level since their initial launch. If concern over the Greek bailout persists, then further buying could follow in the coming week despite the lower prices. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Feb 12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

From the 21st of February, silver ripped higher from $33.50 to a high for the year so far of $37.20 or so on the last day of the month. The main driver for the move was an extremely large increase in long futures positioning. Our recent visit to some of the important Asian markets for silver demonstrate relatively weak industrial demand for the physical metal but investors seemed more interested in the Eldorado (to mix a metaphor) of the $50 target. The sell-off of gold on the 29th was part of a wider $33.25and extremely sudden risk-off move and silver was swept almost $3 lower in a matter of hours. The low that day was $34.15 before silver bounced, along with gold, to a short-lived high of $35.50 on the 1st of March. Since then, though, silver has weakened as the Dollar has strengthened and the price has fallen to $33.25. The main mover for the rise in the silver price was a remarkable 42.2 million ounce increase in net speculative long positioning on COMEX. Positions rose to their largest since early September last year as investors added to long positions and showed their distaste of short positioning or caution in the silver market. Although positioning could certainly rise, it will have fallen since this date as the most recent investors have learnt a valuable lesson. ETF activity was more muted with only 2.9 million ounces of metal purchased by investors. ETF investors tend to have longer term investor horizons than futures investors and the disparity between frantic speculative buying and gentle ETF purchasing suggests that the passion for and expectation of higher prices is more-rooted in technical reasoning than in fundamentals. #### **Silver Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Feb 12**

Although the gap has since increased, it seems likely that another attempt to reach parity will be made sooner rather than later. Looking at movements in the platinum price itself, it gained ground over the end of February and the start of March. With the strike at Impala’s Lease Area now over four weeks old, there was upwards pressure on the platinum price. However, a slowing of the upwards move in the Euro took some of the energy from the market. Platinum’s initial move was a climb from $1,645 on the 21st of February to $1,730 on the 23rd before running out of energy. Platinum weakened, bouncing off the $1,700 level on the 27th and 28th. The real action came on the 29th. Whatever the real reason, a panicky sell-off saw platinum tumble to $1,675, although it did outperform gold even in this fall. With the Impala strike seemingly ending as most of the workforce were re-employed, that driver for higher prices was reduced and platinum has since retraced t

o close to $1,630 under pressure from Dollar strength. - Futures exchange activity in platinum was muted with a 30,000 ounce increase in net long speculative NYMEX positions partially offset by a 20,000 ounce decrease in TOCOM positioning. With investor exposure at its highest level since August 2011, the recent price drop may have prompted a clear-out of the more recent longs. - Platinum ETF holdings increased by more than one tonne in the week to the 2nd of March. They have risen every week so far in 2012, contributing to the strong price rise. We expect buying to continue in the short term. #### **Platinum Exchange Investment Jan 10 — Feb 12** 2,500 2,000

The illegal Impala strike continued to provide some support for higher pgm prices and a relatively firm Euro added some more assistance. Perhaps, though, the $700 level was more important as palladium traded between $700 and $725 for the following week. Even on the 29th as the other metals plummeted, palladium found staunch support at $700. However, with the Dollar strengthen

ing over yet more Greek concerns, palladium has since fallen back to $680. Open interest in palladium on NYMEX increased in the final week of February. Long interest increased as palladium clambered above $700. Net speculative long interest increased by 77,900 ounces to 1.32 million ounces, the longest since September last year. ETF buying interest also continued with more than a tonne of palladium bought by investors in the week to the 2nd of March. Since the start of the year almost 200,000 ounces of metal has flowed into ETF vaults. Although we are not believers in simply annualising flows, it is clear that the scale of buying is one of the reasons for the comparative firmness in the palladium price. #### **Palladium Exchange Investment, Jan 10 — Feb 12** 2,000 1,000
